context.question: (1) Is the child a boy or a girl? (2) How long ere she should be delivered?
context.setting: She desired resolution whether the child she went with was a boy or a girl, and how long it would be before her delivery.

attachments.key_positions: Eight testimonies of a male child against four of a female among the proper significators (1647 count); Saturn, lord of the fifth, in Aries 24°37′; the Moon in Capricorn 9°50′, her distance from the opposition of Saturn being 14°47′; Mercury, lord of the Ascendant, in Aries 11°00′, his distance from the body of Saturn 13°37′; the two distances differing by only one degree ten minutes, and a degree allowed for a week
attachments.note: Positions and testimony counts as printed in the 1647 text; see the ocr_note for the differing count in the 1852 edition.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, Chap. XLII (fifth-house chapter): if with child of a boy or girl, and how long ere delivered (Fig. 11 in the 1852 Zadkiel edition)
provenance.version: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR, auxiliary/christian-astrology-vol1-3_djvu.txt); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition (Introduction to Astrology) and the second OCR (christian-astrology-1647-original_djvu.txt) where noted
